why: After parsing the strings into an undirected unweighted graph, the shortest route from the first listed node to the last is a BFS from the first node; storing each node's parent when discovered lets you rebuild the route and join it with hyphens.
hints: First turn the array into a graph: the count, then N names, then 'A-B' edges. Which traversal finds a fewest-edges path?
BFS from the first name. Record parent[v] when v is first discovered, then walk back from the last name to rebuild the path.
Adjacency dict keyed by name; BFS O(N + E); reverse the parent chain and join with '-'. Return "-1" if the last node was never reached.
pitfalls: Names can contain spaces ("Main Street"); split edges on the hyphen, not on whitespace.
The answer for no path is the string "-1".
